subproblem.title: Admissibility of the regularized unit test field −(χ/√(‖G‖²+η²))·G
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ and ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with the Euclidean norm. Let G : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ be a C¹ vector field. Let χ : ℝⁿ → ℝ be C¹ with compact support and 0 ≤ χ(x) ≤ 1 for all x. Let η > 0 be real, and let g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ satisfy g(x) = −(χ(x)/√(‖G(x)‖² + η²)) • G(x) for every x. Then g is C¹, g has compact support, tsupport g ⊆ tsupport χ, and ‖g(x)‖ ≤ 1 for every x.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : Rn n → Rn n) (χ : Rn n → ℝ) (η : ℝ) (g : Rn n → Rn n), ContDiff ℝ 1 G → ContDiff ℝ 1 χ → HasCompactSupport χ → (∀ x, 0 ≤ χ x ∧ χ x ≤ 1) → 0 < η → (∀ x, g x = -(χ x / Real.sqrt (‖G x‖ ^ 2 + η ^ 2)) • G x) → ContDiff ℝ 1 g ∧ HasCompactSupport g ∧ tsupport g ⊆ tsupport χ ∧ ∀ x, ‖g x‖ ≤ 1
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the selected node's supplied proof, step 3(a)–(c) (Test field). The Riesz gradient ∇w is replaced by an arbitrary C¹ field G, and the cut-off χ is given by hypothesis.
0. Setup. Put N(x) := √(‖G(x)‖² + η²). Since η > 0, ‖G(x)‖² + η² ≥ η² > 0, so N(x) > 0, in particular N(x) ≠ 0, for every x. By the hypothesis on g and function extensionality, g is the function x ↦ −(χ(x)/N(x)) • G(x).
1. g is C¹.
 - x ↦ ‖G(x)‖² is C¹ because G is C¹ (ContDiff.norm_sq; equivalently x ↦ ⟨G(x), G(x)⟩ by ContDiff.inner). Adding the constant η² keeps it C¹.
 - This function never vanishes (step 0), so N is C¹ (ContDiff.sqrt).
 - χ is C¹ and N is C¹ and never 0, so χ/N is C¹ (ContDiff.div), and so is its negative −χ/N.
 - The product of the C¹ scalar function −χ/N with the C¹ vector field G is C¹ (ContDiff.smul). By step 0, g is C¹.
2. support g ⊆ support χ. If χ(x) = 0 then g(x) = −(0/N(x)) • G(x) = 0 • G(x) = 0. Contrapositively, g(x) ≠ 0 implies χ(x) ≠ 0.
3. g has compact support. χ has compact support and support g ⊆ support χ by step 2, so g has compact support (HasCompactSupport.mono): tsupport g is a closed subset of the compact set tsupport χ.
4. tsupport g ⊆ tsupport χ. By step 2 and monotonicity of closure, tsupport g = closure(support g) ⊆ closure(support χ) = tsupport χ.
5. ‖g(x)‖ ≤ 1. Fix x.
 - Since χ(x) ≥ 0 and N(x) > 0, ‖g(x)‖ = |−χ(x)/N(x)|·‖G(x)‖ = χ(x)·‖G(x)‖/N(x) (norm_smul, norm_neg).
 - From ‖G(x)‖² ≤ ‖G(x)‖² + η² and ‖G(x)‖ ≥ 0 we get ‖G(x)‖ ≤ √(‖G(x)‖² + η²) = N(x) (Real.le_sqrt_of_sq_le).
 - With 0 ≤ χ(x) ≤ 1, χ(x)·‖G(x)‖ ≤ 1·‖G(x)‖ ≤ N(x).
 - Dividing by N(x) > 0 (div_le_one) gives ‖g(x)‖ ≤ 1.
6. Conclusion. Steps 1, 3, 4 and 5 are the four claimed properties. ∎
proof_key_steps: N := √(‖G‖² + η²) ≥ η > 0 never vanishes, and g = −(χ/N)•G by function extensionality.
C¹: ‖G‖² + η² is C¹ and nonzero, so N, χ/N and (−χ/N)•G are C¹ (ContDiff.norm_sq, ContDiff.sqrt, ContDiff.div, ContDiff.smul).
χ(x) = 0 ⇒ g(x) = 0, so support g ⊆ support χ; hence g has compact support and tsupport g ⊆ tsupport χ.
‖g(x)‖ = χ(x)‖G(x)‖/N(x) ≤ 1, since 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1 and ‖G(x)‖ ≤ √(‖G(x)‖² + η²) = N(x).

audit.reason: Every hypothesis and all four conclusions match the Lean proposition. Positive η makes the square-root denominator positive everywhere, justifying the C¹ operations. The defining equation yields support containment and compact support. The norm estimate correctly uses both bounds on χ and positivity of the denominator. The proof works for an arbitrary supplied C¹ field G, so no dependency on riesz_gradient is missing.
